liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (2 other sources): This version supplies a One More Saturday Night tease placed before Good Lovin'; Good Lovin' is sandwiched between two parts of One More Saturday Night [2][3]
- **Black Muddy River** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer singles out Black Muddy River as a personal highlight of the show; Black Muddy River is listed as the encore [3][10]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Reviewer finds the opener a bit stale and wants Jerry's solos louder [11]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer remembers Sugaree as particularly fine [14]
- **Iko Iko (start set 2)** (1 review): Reviewer likens Iko Iko to a smooth steam train picking up speed [17]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer feels the show's energy dips after Drums, though the remainder is strong [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **Big River**: cut on the recording [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-02-13.168627.SuperscopeEC-7.ont.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 126 min [1]
- **gd1988-02-13.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.85908.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 129 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd88-02-13.sbd.hinko.24292.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 130 min; rated 3.33/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard sound quality right on, as expected from a soundboard; Reviewer calls the soundboard sound decent; Reviewer praises the soundboard's sound, including the Hammond B-3 organ tone [10][13][17]
- **gd1988-02-13.163694.fob.schoeps.unknown.ebel.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 128 min [5]. Said about its sound: Uploader says this transfer avoids cuts and digital dropouts of earlier versions and sounds better [5]
- **gd88-02-13.aud.wiley.15126.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 121 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [8]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is treble-heavy; reviewer cut treble fully and found enough bass to define the beat [12]

## Around the show

- Reviewer loved the Kaiser; lines were often short, and the park across the street was memorable in cold, dark winter [15]
- The following nights fell on Valentine's Day, Mardi Gras and Chinese New Year [15]
- Uploader prefers the Kaiser because it was smaller than the Oakland Coliseum Arena [1]
- Uploader's first Dead show was at the Kaiser on Feb 9 1986, seated in the tapers section [1]
- Muffled noise during Looks Like Rain came from the mics being put in a bag to avoid a bust [5]
- One of four shows in five nights, and the only one not on a holiday [15]
- Reviewer treats it as a tour opener and judges it a decent one [16]
- Reviewer says the sets are fairly typical of the late 1980s [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-02-13.168627.SuperscopeEC-7.ont.flac1644**: taped by OldNeumanntapr; transferred by OldNeumanntapr; source: OTS; Superscope EC-7 Cardioids (Near Coincident) >Sony TC-153SD [XLIIS] [1]
- **gd1988-02-13.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.85908.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5/TDK MA-R90) D [2]. Also: Schoeps CMC3/MK41 microphones to DAT to CD; tapes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [2]
- **gd88-02-13.sbd.hinko.24292.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [3]. Also: Soundboard to MC to DAT to CD, then EAC and SHN conversion by Darryl Hinko [3]
- **gd1988-02-13.163694.fob.schoeps.unknown.ebel.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Pete Ebel; source: FOB Schoeps CMC 3 MK4-> PCM-> DAT [5]. Also: New DAT transfer by Pete Ebel, from the same Schoeps source as two earlier versions [5]
- **gd88-02-13.aud.wiley.15126.sbeok.shnf**: source: Schoeps CMC3/MK41>Dat>CDR [8]
